title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operating in Austin struck and killed a duck in its path without slowing or stopping. The vehicle was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, meaning the system encountered an obstacle it did not avoid and the operator did not intervene. It is not established whether the vehicle's perception system failed to detect the duck, whether it detected but misclassified the obstacle, or whether its planning system chose not to stop.

The incident reveals a gap between what autonomous vehicles are designed to do and what happens when they encounter small animals on roadways. A system that must share urban streets with pedestrians and wildlife had not been tested or trained sufficiently to handle this class of obstacle. Whether human oversight could have prevented this particular death depends on whether the operator had time to react, which is not established.

A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, but Avride disputed this after reviewing data. The company's response was to exclude certain streets from its test routes and to conduct simulation experiments aimed at improving performance, rather than to establish what the vehicle's actual behavior was at the stop sign.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern about self-driving car technology. The incident occurred when the vehicle, which was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without stopping or slowing down. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant and was familiar to residents, intensifying their reaction to the incident. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

Following the incident, Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets near the lake from its autonomous vehicle routes. The company is conducting controlled experiments in simulation to improve the technology and prevent similar situations without compromising safety performance. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Zoox, Tesla, and Waymo, continue testing and operating commercial services in Austin.
